newsitem.title: UK: Gilts relinquish early gains but spread narrows.
newsitem.headline: Gilts relinquish early gains but spread narrows.

text.p: Gilt futures endured a topsy-turvy session, ending virtually flat having traded more than half-a-point higher at one stage.

But with Bunds easing off, the UK market locked in some spread gains suggesting its recent bout of underperformance may have drawn to a close. "We narrowed the spread really quite dramatically from Wednesday through this morning, to a low of 171 basis points," said a senior salesman at a UK brokerage.
"That got the market as close to overbought as we've seen for a while."
The December future settled at 108-18, up just 3/32 on the day and well below a 109-02 high set in the morning. That represented a new contract high.
The gilt/Bund spread stood at 173 basis points in late trade. On Wednesday, it had stretched as wide as 183.
But after gilts spiked higher early on Friday, buying dried up. "We saw some switching shorter and selling at those levels. And no new buying came in," the salesman said.
Nonetheless, the underperformance that has plagued gilts could be over for now. Economists said gilts had suffered after last weekend's meeting of European Union leaders in Ireland.

Analysts said agreement on a fiscal stability pact and a new exchange rate mechanism meant the nuts and bolts of European Economic and Monetary Union were being tackled and suggested the intended start date of January 1, 1999 remained on track.
That prompted a wave of convergence trades by Europe's more peripheral bond markets over Bunds. But the UK's opt-out clause from a single currency left gilts out in the cold.

But they may now be catching up. "It's about time," said Steve Scott, gilts analyst at Kleinwort Benson. "There was always going to be support for gilts above 180. The intraday peak of 183 earlier this week probably lured buyers back in."
The fact that Swedish bonds were trading well through gilts and Spanish bonds got close to doing the same had prompted investors to re-evaluate, he said.
"There's probably another 10 basis points of narrowing for gilts (over Bunds) in the medium-term."
The salesman added that the strong possibility of the next UK government being a Labour one had profound implications for the premium at which gilts trade to Bunds.
"You have to ask what the next government is going to be. If it's Labour and they commit Britain to EMU, you have to think the spread is far too wide," he said.

Short sterling futures rallied in sympathy with the gilt early on Friday but held on to their gains slightly more successfully. The December future gained two basis points to 94.03 while the March contract rose three to 93.89.
